tickets.title: Design the scheduled-export settings screen
tickets.description:
Users can export a report once, but not on a schedule. Add a settings screen where a saved report can be given a cadence, a delivery channel and a recipient list.

Out of scope: the delivery worker itself — that is DEMO-220.
acceptanceCriteria: A saved report can be given a daily, weekly or monthly cadence
Recipients are validated against the directory before the schedule saves
Turning a schedule off keeps its history and does not delete the saved report
Screen passes the WCAG 2.2 AA contrast and keyboard checks
tickets.aiSummary:
Build the settings surface for scheduled exports — cadence, channel and recipients for an already-saved report. The delivery mechanism is a separate ticket, so this is UI plus validation and persistence, not plumbing.

From linked docs
  • Reporting RFC §4 — schedules are stored against the saved report, not the user, so a shared report keeps one schedule.
  • The RFC fixes the cadence set at three values; anything finer needs a capacity review first.
Related tickets
  • DEMO-220 (In Progress) — the delivery worker that will read these rows.
Watch out for
  • Recipient validation hits the directory API, which rate-limits at 10 req/s — batch the check.
tickets.proposedSolution:
• Add a report_schedules table keyed by saved-report id.
  • New settings panel reusing the existing form primitives.
  • Batch the directory lookup behind one validate endpoint.
tickets.effortEstimate: 4–5 days — the form is routine; recipient validation and the shared-report edge case carry the risk.
openQuestions: Does a shared report let every viewer edit the schedule, or only the owner?
Do we need a per-tenant cap on scheduled exports?

confluence.title: Reporting RFC
confluence.excerpt: Schedules belong to the saved report. Cadence is limited to daily / weekly / monthly in v1.

externalLinks.title: Figma — export settings

tickets.description: The nightly export for the largest tenant exceeds the 30-minute job budget roughly one night in three. Blocked: we need the capacity numbers from the platform team before choosing between sharding and a longer budget.
acceptanceCriteria: Nightly export completes inside the job budget for every tenant
A run that does exceed it alerts instead of failing silently
openQuestions: When can platform give us the per-node capacity figures?
Is a 60-minute budget acceptable to operations?

tickets.aiSummary:
The nightly export for the largest tenant overruns its 30-minute budget about one night in three. The ticket is Blocked on per-node capacity numbers from the platform team, and the fix (#412) has changes requested: the third retry can outlast the budget.

Code / PRs
  • #412 — serialiser change and retry backoff. 0 approvals, 5 unresolved comments.

Evidence from linked systems

  • Dynatrace: the linked trace has 6 failed spans out of 38, and the failure originates in object-storage-gateway: PUT /exports/{id} (HTTP 504 ×4 · 500 ×2, SocketTimeoutException: Read timed out ×4, slowest span 30.0 s). The linked Davis problem P-24100731 (response time degradation) is CLOSED.

What this means: the timeouts sit in the storage call, not in the serialiser the PR changes — worth settling together with the capacity numbers before choosing between sharding and a longer budget.

tickets.title: Delivery worker for scheduled exports
tickets.description: Reads due schedules and delivers the rendered export to its channel. Retries with backoff; a permanently failing schedule pauses itself and notifies the owner.
acceptanceCriteria: Due schedules are picked up within one minute
Transient failures retry three times with backoff
A schedule that fails three runs in a row pauses and notifies its owner
tickets.aiSummary:
The engine behind scheduled exports: poll for due schedules, render, deliver, retry. Infrastructure is already merged (#431); the worker itself is in review with open comments.

Code / PRs
  • #430 — worker loop and retry policy. Three unresolved comments, all on the backoff maths.
  • #431 — queue and IAM, merged two days ago.
Watch out for
  • The pause-and-notify path has no test yet; it is the acceptance criterion most likely to be missed.

tickets.title: Chase the data-retention sign-off
Signed download links for exported files
tickets.description:
Export downloads are currently unauthenticated URLs with a guessable path. Replace them with short-lived signed links scoped to the requesting user.

Security: this also closes what Checkmarx reported on the old download path — Path_Traversal in the download controller, and CVE-2022-23529 through jsonwebtoken@8.5.1, upgraded to 9.0.2.
acceptanceCriteria: Links expire after 15 minutes
A link issued for one user cannot be used by another
Expired links return 403, never the file
tickets.aiSummary:
Replaces guessable export URLs with 15-minute signed links scoped to the requesting user. PR #425 has two approvals and no open comments.

Evidence from linked systems

  • Checkmarx: compared with main, CVE-2022-23529 and the jsonwebtoken 8.5.1 package are gone on the branch (fixed). The Path_Traversal finding at /src/export/DownloadController.java:88 is still open.

What this means: the dependency fix is verified, but the ticket also names a path-traversal finding that is still open on the branch — confirm it is out of scope, or fix it, before merging.

confluence.title: Link signing standard
confluence.excerpt: HMAC-SHA256 over path + user id + expiry. 15 minutes is the platform default.

tickets.aiSummary:
Switches the saved-reports list to keyset pagination so it stops loading every report at once. The first attempt (offset paging, #418) was declined for skew problems; this one is in review.

Code / PRs
  • #426 — keyset paging for the list endpoint. 1 approval, 4 of 11 comments still open.

Evidence from linked systems

  • Jenkins: the QA build #88 failed at Integration tests — 3 of 296 tests fail: SavedReportPagingTest.lastPageIsPartial (expected 7 rows on the last page, got 0), SavedReportPagingTest.cursorSurvivesRefresh (the cursor no longer matches the sort key) and ApiContractTest.pageSizeCapped (page size 250, cap 100).

What this means: all three failures are in the paging code this PR adds, not in the environment — fix them before asking for another review.
